paragraphs: We are engaged primarily in two business segments: movie theatres and hotels and resorts.

As of December 31, 2025, our theatre operations included 78 movie theatres with 985 screens throughout 17 states (Wisconsin, Illinois, Iowa, Minnesota, Missouri, Nebraska, North Dakota, Ohio, Arkansas, Colorado, Georgia, Kentucky, Louisiana, New York, Pennsylvania, Texas and Virginia), including one movie theatre with 14 screens in Minnesota owned by a third party and managed by us. Our movie theatres operate under the Marcus Theatres, Movie Tavern by Marcus, and BistroPlex brands. We also operate a family entertainment center, Funset Boulevard, that is adjacent to one of our theatres in Appleton, Wisconsin. As of the date of this Annual Report, we are the 4th largest theatre circuit in the United States.

As of December 31, 2025, our hotels and resorts operations included seven wholly-owned and operated hotels and resorts in Wisconsin, Illinois, and Nebraska. We also manage nine hotels, resorts and other properties for our joint ventures and third parties in Wisconsin, California, Minnesota, Nevada, Nebraska, Illinois, Iowa, and Pennsylvania. As of December 31, 2025, we owned or managed approximately 4,700 hotel and resort rooms.

Both of these business segments are discussed in detail below. For information regarding the revenues, operating income or loss, assets and certain other financial information of these segments for the last three full fiscal years, please see our consolidated financial statements and the accompanying Note 12 in Part II below.
Please see our discussion under "Current Plans" in Item 7 – Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations.

At the end of fiscal 2025, we owned or operated 78 movie theatre locations with a total of 985 screens in Wisconsin, Illinois, Iowa, Minnesota, Missouri, Nebraska, North Dakota, Ohio, Arkansas, Colorado, Georgia, Kentucky, Louisiana, New York, Pennsylvania, Texas and Virginia. Included in our portfolio is a single movie theatre location with 14 screens in Minnesota that we manage for a third party. We averaged 12.6 screens per location at the end of fiscal 2025, 2024 and 2023. Our 77 company-owned facilities include 46 megaplex theatres (12 or more screens), representing approximately 71% of our total screens, 30 multiplex theatres (two to 11 screens) and one single-screen theatre.

We invested approximately $340 million, excluding acquisitions, to further enhance the movie-going experience and amenities in new and existing theatres over the last ten years. These investments include:

New theatres. In October 2019, we opened the eight-screen Movie Tavern® by Marcus theatre in Brookfield, Wisconsin. This theatre became the first Movie Tavern by Marcus in Wisconsin. It includes eight auditoriums, each with laser projection and comfortable DreamLoungerSM recliner seating, a full-service bar and food and drink center, and a delivery-to-seat service model that also allows guests to order food and beverage via our mobile app/web, in-seat QR code or in-theatre kiosk. We will consider additional sites for potential new theatre locations in both new and existing markets in the future.

Theatre acquisitions. In addition to building new theatres, acquisitions of existing theatres or theatre circuits has also been a viable growth strategy for us. In 2019, we acquired the assets of Movie Tavern®, a New Orleans-based industry leading circuit known for its in-theatre dining concept featuring chef-driven menus, premium quality food and drink and luxury seating. Now branded Movie Tavern by Marcus, the acquired circuit consisted of 208 screens at 22 locations in nine states – Arkansas, Colorado, Georgia, Kentucky, Louisiana, New York, Pennsylvania, Texas and Virginia. The acquisition of the Movie Tavern circuit increased our total number of screens at that time by an additional 23%. We also have entered into management agreements with third parties which allow us to promote our brand and may lead to opportunities to own additional theatres. In fiscal 2024, we entered into an agreement to assume operations of the West End Cinema, a 14 screen theatre in St. Louis Park, Minnesota.

We will continue to consider potential acquisitions as well as consider management agreements. The movie theatre industry is very fragmented, with approximately 50% of United States screens owned by the three largest theatre circuits and the other 50% owned by hundreds of smaller operators, making it very difficult to predict when acquisition opportunities may arise. We do not believe that we are geographically constrained, and we believe that we may be able to add value to certain theatres through our various proprietary amenities and operating expertise.

DreamLounger recliner additions. These luxurious, state-of-the-art recliners allow guests to go from upright to a full-recline position in seconds. These seat changes require full auditorium remodels to accommodate the necessary 84 inches of legroom, resulting in the loss of approximately 50% of the existing traditional seats in an average auditorium. To date, the addition of DreamLoungers has increased attendance in the years following installation at each of our applicable theatres, outperforming nearby competitive theatres and growing the overall market attendance in most cases. During fiscal 2024, we added DreamLounger seating at one Movie Tavern theatre. As of December 31, 2025, we offered all DreamLounger recliner seating in 66 theatres, representing approximately 86% of our company-owned theatres. Including our premium, large format (PLF) auditoriums with recliner seating, as of December 31, 2025, we offered our DreamLounger recliner seating in approximately 88% of our company-owned screens, a percentage we believe to be the highest among the largest theatre chains in the nation.

UltraScreen DLX®, SuperScreen DLX® (DreamLounger eXperience) and ScreenX conversions. We introduced one of the first PLF presentations to the industry when we rolled out our proprietary UltraScreen® concept over 25 years ago. We later introduced our UltraScreen DLX concept by combining our premium, large-format presentation with DreamLounger recliner seating and Dolby® Atmos™ immersive sound to elevate the movie-going experience for our guests. Most of our PLF screens now include the added feature of heated DreamLounger recliner seats. In fiscal 2023, we introduced our first ScreenX auditorium featuring 270-degree projection providing guests with an immersive viewing experience. From fiscal 2019 through fiscal 2025, we converted one existing screen at an acquired theatre to UltraScreen DLX, opened one new UltraScreen DLX at an acquired theatre, converted 38 existing screens to SuperScreen DLX, opened one new SuperScreen DLX auditorium at a newly built Movie Tavern by Marcus theatre, and converted four existing screens to ScreenX. As of December 31, 2025, we had 31 UltraScreen DLX auditoriums, one traditional UltraScreen auditorium, 87 SuperScreen DLX auditoriums (a slightly smaller screen than an UltraScreen but with the same DreamLounger seating and Dolby Atmos sound), four ScreenX and three IMAX® PLF screens at 64 of our theatre locations. As of December 31, 2025, we offered at least one PLF screen in approximately 83% of our company-owned theatres – once again a percentage we believe to be the highest percentage among the largest theatre chains in the nation. Our PLF screens generally have higher per-screen revenues and draw customers from a larger geographic region compared to our standard screens, and we charge a premium price to our guests for this experience. We continue to evaluate opportunities to convert additional existing screens to SuperScreen DLX or ScreenX.

Signature cocktail and dining concepts. We have continued to further enhance our food and beverage offerings within our existing theatres. We believe our nearly 70 years of food and beverage experience in the hotel and restaurant businesses provides us with a unique advantage and expertise that we can leverage to further grow revenues in our theatres. The concepts we offer include:

•Take Five® Lounge, Take Five Express and The Tavern – These full-service bars offer an inviting atmosphere and a chef-inspired dining menu, along with a complete selection of cocktails, locally-brewed beers and wines. We also offer full liquor service through the concession stand at two theatres. We operate 18 bars known as The Tavern. As of December 31, 2025, we offered bars/full liquor service at 48 theatres, representing approximately 62% of our company-owned theatres.

headings: Operational Risks
The lack of both the quantity and audience appeal of motion pictures may adversely affect our financial results.
A deterioration in relationships with or consolidation of film distributors could adversely affect our ability to obtain commercially successful films or increase our costs to obtain such films.
The relative industry supply of available rooms at comparable lodging facilities may adversely affect our financial results.
Each of our business segments and properties experience ongoing intense competition.
Changes in the availability of and the cost of labor could adversely affect our business.
Supply chain disruptions may negatively impact our operating results.
Adverse weather conditions, particularly during the winter in the Midwest and in our other markets, may adversely affect our financial results.
Our results are seasonal, resulting in unpredictable and varied quarterly results.
Our properties are subject to risks relating to acts of God, terrorist activity and war and any such event may adversely affect our financial results.
If the amount of sales made through third-party internet travel intermediaries increases significantly, consumer loyalty to our hotels could decrease and our revenues could fall.
Financial Risks
Adverse economic conditions in our markets may adversely affect our financial results.
Our businesses are heavily capital intensive and preopening and start-up costs, increasing depreciation expenses and impairment charges may adversely affect our financial results.

We may not be able to obtain capital when desired on favorable terms, if at all, and we may not be able to obtain capital or complete acquisitions through the use of equity or without dilution to our shareholders.
Our ability to pay dividends or repurchase common stock may be limited or otherwise restricted.
Servicing our debt requires a significant amount of cash, and we may not have sufficient cash flow from our business to repay our debt.
Strategic Risks
We may not achieve the expected benefits and performance of our strategic initiatives and acquisitions.
Our ability to identify suitable properties to acquire, develop and manage will directly impact our ability to achieve certain of our growth objectives.

Our ability to identify suitable joint venture partners or raise investment funds to acquire, develop and manage hotels and resorts will directly impact our ability to achieve certain of our growth objectives.
Investing through partnerships or joint ventures decreases our ability to manage risk.
Legal, Regulatory and Compliance Risks
Recalls of food products and associated costs could adversely affect our reputation and financial condition.
We are subject to substantial government regulation, which could entail significant cost.
We are subject to complex taxation and could be subject to changes in our tax rates, the adoption of new tax legislation or exposure to additional tax liabilities.
General Risks
Our stock price may be volatile, which could result in securities class action litigation against us.
Certain provisions of our articles of incorporation and bylaws and of Wisconsin law could prevent a takeover that shareholders consider favorable and could also reduce the market price of our stock.
paragraphs: The following risk factors and other information included in this Annual Report on Form 10-K should be carefully considered. The risks and uncertainties described below are not the only ones we face. Additional risks and uncertainties not presently known to us or that we currently deem immaterial also may impair our business operations. If any of the following risks occur, our business, financial condition, operating results, and cash flows could be materially adversely affected.

A pandemic or epidemic may have a material adverse effect on our theatre and hotels and resorts businesses, results of operations, liquidity, cash flows, financial condition, access to credit markets and ability to service our existing and future indebtedness, and future pandemics or epidemics may have similar material adverse effects in the future.

The COVID-19 pandemic had an unprecedented impact on both of our business segments. As an operator of movie theatres, hotels and resorts, restaurants and bars, each of which consists of spaces where customers and guests gather in close proximity, our businesses were significantly impacted by protective actions that federal, state and local governments took to control the spread of the pandemic. These actions included, among other things, declaring national and state emergencies, encouraging social distancing, restricting freedom of movement and congregation, mandating non-essential business closures and/or capacity restrictions, issuing shelter-in-place, quarantine and stay-at-home orders, and issuing masking and/or vaccination mandates.

We cannot predict if a similar or different pandemic or epidemic may occur again in the future. The longer and more severe the outbreak of infectious disease, including repeat or cyclical outbreaks or future pandemics or epidemics, the more severe the adverse effects will be on our businesses, results of operations, liquidity, cash flows, financial condition, access to credit markets and ability to service our existing and future indebtedness.

Fears and concerns regarding future pandemics could cause our customers to again avoid assembling in public spaces, even in the absence of government directives or restrictions. We would have no control over and cannot predict the length of any future required closure of or restrictions on our theatres and hotels and resorts due to future pandemics or epidemics. If we are unable to generate revenues due to a future prolonged period of closure, this would negatively impact our ability to remain in compliance with our debt covenants, meet our payment obligations and fund capital projects. In such an event, we would either seek covenant waivers or attempt to amend our debt covenants, though there is no certainty that we would be successful in such efforts. If we are not successful in such efforts, our lenders could declare a default and require immediate repayment of amounts owing under our Credit Agreement and senior notes, which could have a material adverse effect on our ability to operate our business. Additionally, we could seek additional liquidity through the issuance of new debt or equity. Our ability to obtain additional financing and the terms of any such additional financing would depend in part on factors outside of our control, and we may be unable to obtain such additional financing on acceptable terms or at all.

The financial results of our movie theatre business and the motion picture industry in general are heavily dependent on the general audience appeal of available films, together with studio marketing, advertising and support campaigns, factors over which we have no control. The relative success of our movie theatre business will continue to be largely dependent upon the quantity and audience appeal of films made available by the movie studios and other producers. Poor performance of films, a disruption in the production of films due to events such as a strike by actors, writers or directors, or a reduction in the marketing efforts of the film distributors to promote their films could have an adverse impact on our business and results of operations. Our industry experienced a significant reduction in the quantity of films available to exhibit in theatres in the years following the COVID-19 pandemic. The quantity of new film releases available for theatrical exhibition during fiscal 2023 and fiscal 2024 was negatively impacted by the shutdown of movie production during the Writers Guild of America (WGA) and Screen Actors Guild - American Federation of Television and Radio Artists (SAG-AFTRA) labor strikes that occurred during fiscal 2023. Studios may also determine that certain types of films will not be released for theatrical exhibition and will go straight to streaming services, further impacting the quantity of films available. Also, our quarterly results of operations are significantly dependent on the quantity and audience appeal of films that we exhibit during each quarter. As a result, our quarterly results may be unpredictable and somewhat volatile.

paragraphs: Beginning in fiscal 2025, our fiscal year changed to a fiscal year ending on December 31 of each year. Fiscal 2025 was a 370 operating day year beginning on December 27, 2024 and ending on December 31, 2025 (comprised of five operating days between December 27-31, 2024, plus 365 operating days in calendar year 2025). Accordingly, for our fiscal year ended December 31, 2025, our quarterly results were for three month periods ended March 31, June 30, September 30 and December 31.

For fiscal 2024 and prior periods, we reported our consolidated and individual segment results of operations on a 52- or 53-week fiscal year ending on the last Thursday in December, dividing our fiscal year into three 13-week quarters and a final quarter consisting of 13 or 14 weeks. Fiscal 2024 was a 52-week year with 364 operating days, beginning on December 29, 2023 and ending on December 26, 2024. Fiscal 2023 was a 52-week year with 364 operating days, beginning on December 30, 2022 and ending on December 28, 2023.

Fiscal 2026 will be a 365 operating day year beginning on January 1, 2026 and ending on December 31, 2026, with quarterly results for the three month periods ending March 31, June 30, September 30 and December 31.

Our first fiscal quarter typically produces the weakest operating results in our hotels and resorts division due primarily to the effects of reduced travel during the winter months. The quality of film product in any given quarter typically impacts the operating results in our theatre division. Our second and third fiscal quarters generally produce our strongest operating results because these periods coincide with the typical summer seasonality of the movie theatre industry and the summer strength of the lodging business. Due to the fact that the week between Christmas and New Year's Eve is historically one of the strongest weeks of the year for our theatre division, the specific timing of the last Thursday in December has historically impacted the results of our fiscal first and fourth quarters in that division. Due to the transition in our fiscal year during fiscal 2025 described above, the first quarter of fiscal 2025 included five days during the week between Christmas and New Year's Eve, and the fourth quarter of fiscal 2025 included the entire week between Christmas and New Year's Eve.

Our primary operations are reported in two business segments: theatres and hotels and resorts. This Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations ("MD&A") generally discusses fiscal 2025 and

fiscal 2024 items and year-to-year comparisons between fiscal 2025 and fiscal 2024. Discussions of fiscal 2023 items and year-to-year comparisons between fiscal 2024 and fiscal 2023 that are not included in this MD&A can be found in "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations" in Part II, Item 7 of the Company's Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 26, 2024. Within this MD&A amounts for totals, subtotals, and variances may not recalculate exactly within tables due to rounding as they are calculated using the unrounded numbers.

Our aggregate cash capital expenditures, acquisitions and net purchases of interests in, and contributions to, joint ventures were $83.2 million during fiscal 2025, compared to $83.3 million during fiscal 2024 and $38.8 million during fiscal 2023. We currently estimate that cash capital expenditures during fiscal 2026 will be in the $50 - $55 million range, with significant investments in our hotels division now behind us as discussed below. We will, however, continue to monitor our operating results and economic and industry conditions so that we may adjust our plans accordingly.
Our current strategic plans include the following goals and strategies: Theatres

•Maximize and leverage our current assets. We have invested approximately $340 million to further enhance the movie-going experience and amenities in new and existing theatres over the last ten years. These investments have included:

◦DreamLoungerSM recliner seating additions. As of December 31, 2025, we offered all DreamLounger recliner seating in 66 theatres, representing approximately 86% of our company-owned theatres. Including our premium, large format (PLF) auditoriums with recliner seating, as of December 31, 2025, we offered our DreamLounger recliner seating in approximately 88% of our company-owned screens, a percentage we believe to be the highest among the largest theatre chains in the nation.

◦UltraScreen DLX®, SuperScreen DLX® (DreamLounger eXperience) and ScreenX conversions. As of December 31, 2025, we had a total of 126 PLF screens at 64 of our theatre locations (31 UltraScreen DLX auditoriums, one traditional UltraScreen® auditorium, 87 SuperScreen DLX auditoriums - a slightly smaller screen than an UltraScreen but with the same DreamLounger seating and Dolby Atmos sound - four ScreenX auditoriums, and three IMAX® PLF screens). In fiscal 2023, we introduced our first ScreenX auditorium featuring 270-degree projection providing guests with an immersive viewing experience, and we added three additional ScreenX auditoriums at additional theatres in fiscal 2025. As of December 31, 2025, we offered at least one PLF screen in approximately 83% of our company-owned theatres, once again a percentage we believe to be the highest percentage among the largest theatre chains in the nation. In addition, as of December 31, 2025 we offered more than one PLF screen in approximately 62% of our company-owned theatres, which we believe gives us significant operational flexibility to maximize revenue by showing more than one major film on PLF screens at a theatre, particularly during opening weekends for films and at peak times during the year. Our PLF screens generally have higher per-screen revenues and draw customers from a larger geographic region compared to our standard screens, and we charge a premium price to our guests for this experience.

◦Signature cocktail and dining concepts. We have continued to further enhance our food and beverage offerings within our existing theatres. We believe our 50-plus years of food and beverage experience in the hotel and restaurant businesses provides us with a unique advantage and expertise that we can leverage to further grow revenues in our theatres. As of December 31, 2025, we offered bars/full liquor service under the concepts Take Five Lounge, Take Five Express and The Tavern at 48 theatres, representing approximately 62% of our company-owned theatres. In select locations without a Take Five Lounge outlet, we offer beer and wine at the Zaffiro's Express outlet. As of December 31, 2025, we also offered one or more in-lobby dining concepts, including the pizza concept Zaffiro's® Express and hamburger and other Americana fare concept Reel Sizzle, in 39 theatres, representing approximately 68%
of our company-owned theatres (excluding our in-theatre dining theatres). We also operate three Zaffiro's® Pizzeria and Bar full-service restaurants.

◦In-theatre dining concepts. As of December 31, 2025, we offered a complete menu of drinks and chef-prepared salads, sandwiches, entrées and desserts at 20 theatres, representing approximately 26% of our company-owned theatres, through two service models. At 14 theatres we offer in-theatre dining operating under the BistroPlex® and Movie Tavern by Marcus brands with ordering at the bar, online, mobile app/web, and in select locations with servers, for food delivery to seats. In addition, at 6 theatres with in-theatre dining operating under the Movie Tavern by Marcus and Marcus Theatres brands, we also offer the same complete menu available to order at the concession stand in addition to ordering with online, mobile app/web for delivery to seats or pickup at the concession stand.

paragraphs: 本公司主要從事兩個業務分部：電影院與飯店及度假村。

截至2025年12月31日，我們的電影院運營包含17個州（威斯康辛州、伊利諾州、愛荷華州、明尼蘇達州、密蘇裏州、內布拉斯加州、北達科他州、俄亥俄州、阿肯色州、科羅拉多州、佐治亞州、肯塔基州、路易斯安那州、紐約州、賓夕法尼亞州、德州與弗吉尼亞州）的78家電影院，共計985個銀幕，其中包括一間由第三方所有、由本公司管理的位於明尼蘇達州、擁有14個銀幕的電影院。我們的電影院運營採用Marcus Theatres、Movie Tavern by Marcus與BistroPlex品牌。我們也運營一家家庭娛樂中心Funset Boulevard，位於威斯康辛州阿普爾頓市的一間電影院旁。截至本年度報告日，我們是美國第四大電影院連鎖體系。
截至2025年12月31日，我們的飯店及度假村運營包含在威斯康辛州、伊利諾州與內布拉斯加州的七間完全擁有並運營的飯店與度假村。我們也為我們的合資企業與第三方在威斯康辛州、加州、明尼蘇達州、內華達州、內布拉斯加州、伊利諾州、愛荷華州與賓夕法尼亞州管理九間飯店、度假村及其他財產。截至2025年12月31日，我們擁有或管理約4,700間飯店與度假村客房。
這兩個業務分部皆於下文詳細說明。有關這兩個分部在最近三個完整會計年度的收入、營運收入或虧損、資產及某些其他財務資訊，請參閱我們的合併財務報表及附註第12項於第二部分下方。
請參閱我們在第7項「管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之分析」下的「目前計畫」討論。

截至2025會計年度末，我們擁有或運營78間電影院，總計985個銀幕，位於威斯康辛州、伊利諾州、愛荷華州、明尼蘇達州、密蘇裏州、內布拉斯加州、北達科他州、俄亥俄州、阿肯色州、科羅拉多州、佐治亞州、肯塔基州、路易斯安那州、紐約州、賓夕法尼亞州、德州與弗吉尼亞州。我們的資產中包含一間由第三方所有、由本公司管理的位於明尼蘇達州、擁有14個銀幕的電影院。截至2025、2024與2023會計年度末，我們平均每間電影院擁有12.6個銀幕。我們的77間自有設施包含46間超級電影院（12個或更多銀幕），佔我們總銀幕數的約71%，30間多銀幕電影院（2至11個銀幕）與一間單銀幕電影院。
{'translated_text': '我們投資約 340 百萬美元，不計併購，以進一步提升過去十年新舊戲院的觀影體驗與設施。這些投資包括：'}

新電影院。2019年10月，我們在威斯康辛州布魯克菲爾德市開幕了八銀幕的Movie Tavern® by Marcus電影院。這間電影院成為首間位於威斯康辛州的Movie Tavern by Marcus電影院。該電影院包含八間劇場，每間皆配備雷射投影與舒適的DreamLoungerSM recliner座椅，並設有全服務酒吧與餐飲中心，以及提供餐飲至座位的服務模式，也允許顧客透過手機應用程式/網頁、座位QR碼或電影院內的服務臺點餐飲。我們將在未來考慮在新舊市場中潛在的新電影院地點。

戲院收購。除了興建新戲院，收購現有戲院或戲院路線也一直是我們可持續成長的策略之一。2019年，我們收購了位於紐奧良的Movie Tavern®，這是一家在業界領先的戲院路線，以戲院內用餐概念聞名，提供由主廚策劃的餐點、高品質的飲食與豪華座椅。現已重新品牌為Movie Tavern by Marcus，收購的戲院路線包含22個據點，共208個銀幕，分佈於九個州 – 阿肯色州、科羅拉多州、喬治亞州、肯塔基州、路易斯安那州、紐約州、賓州、德州與維吉尼亞州。收購Movie Tavern路線使我們當時的總銀幕數增加約23%。我們也與第三方簽訂管理協議，允許我們推廣品牌，並可能帶來擁有更多戲院的機會。在會計年度2024，我們與第三方簽訂協議，接管位於明尼蘇達州聖路易斯帕克的West End Cinema，這是一個擁有14個銀幕的戲院。
我們會持續評估潛在收購機會以及管理協議。電影戲院產業非常分散，美國約有50%的銀幕由三大戲院路線擁有，其餘50%則由數百家較小的經營者擁有，因此很難預測收購機會何時會出現。我們不認為自己受到地理限制，我們相信透過我們各種專利設施與營運專業，可以為某些戲院增加價值。

DreamLounger躺椅增設。這些豪華、最先進的躺椅讓顧客能在幾秒內從坐直姿轉換為完全躺平姿勢。這些座椅變換需要整座劇場進行翻修，以容納必要的84英寸腿部空間，導致平均劇場中約50%的傳統座椅被取代。截至目前為止，DreamLounger的增設在安裝後的幾年內，使我們適用的戲院的入場人數增加，表現優於附近競爭對手，並在大多數情況下擴大整體市場入場人數。在會計年度2024，我們在一個Movie Tavern戲院增設了DreamLounger座椅。截至2025年12月31日，我們在66個戲院提供所有DreamLounger躺椅座椅，約佔我們自有戲院的86%。包含我們的豪華大格式（PLF）劇場與躺椅座椅，截至2025年12月31日，我們在約88%的自有銀幕提供DreamLounger躺椅座椅，我們相信這個比例在全國最大的戲院連鎖中是最高的。

UltraScreen DLX®、SuperScreen DLX®（DreamLounger eXperience）與ScreenX轉換。我們在25年前推出我們專利的UltraScreen®概念，成為業界首個PLF（豪華大格式）放映。我們後續推出UltraScreen DLX概念，結合我們的豪華大格式放映與DreamLounger躺椅座椅與Dolby® Atmos™沉浸式音效，以提升顧客的觀影體驗。我們大多數的PLF銀幕現在都包含加裝的加熱DreamLounger躺椅座椅。在會計年度2023，我們推出首個ScreenX劇場，提供270度投影，為顧客帶來沉浸式觀影體驗。從會計年度2019至2025，我們將一個現有銀幕轉換為UltraScreen DLX，於一個收購的戲院開設一個新的UltraScreen DLX，將38個現有銀幕轉換為SuperScreen DLX，於一個新建的Movie Tavern by Marcus戲院開設一個新的SuperScreen DLX劇場，並將四個現有銀幕轉換為ScreenX。截至2025年12月31日，我們擁有31個UltraScreen DLX劇場，一個傳統UltraScreen劇場，87個SuperScreen DLX劇場（螢幕尺寸略小於UltraScreen，但擁有相同的DreamLounger座椅與Dolby Atmos音效），4個ScreenX與3個IMAX® PLF銀幕，位於64個戲院據點。截至2025年12月31日，我們在約83%的自有戲院提供至少一個PLF銀幕 – 這比例我們相信在全國最大的戲院連鎖中是最高的。我們的PLF銀幕通常每銀幕收入較高，吸引來自較大地理範圍的顧客，我們也對顧客收取較高的價格以換取此體驗。我們持續評估將更多現有銀幕轉換為SuperScreen DLX或ScreenX的機會。
特色雞尾酒與用餐概念。我們持續提升現有戲院中的餐飲服務。我們相信我們在酒店與餐飲業近70年的餐飲經驗，為我們在戲院中進一步成長收入提供了獨特的優勢與專業知識。我們提供的概念包括：
•Take Five® Lounge、Take Five Express與The Tavern – 這些全服務酒吧提供舒適的氛圍與由主廚策劃的餐點，並提供完整的雞尾酒、本地釀造啤酒與葡萄酒選擇。我們也在兩間戲院的售票處提供完整的酒類服務。我們經營18間稱為The Tavern的酒吧。截至2025年12月31日，我們在48間戲院提供酒吧/酒類服務，約佔我們自有戲院的62%。

paragraphs: 自財務年度2025年起，本公司財務年度改為每年12月31日為結算日。財務年度2025為一個包含370個營運日的年度，自2024年12月27日起至2025年12月31日為止（包含2024年12月27日至12月31日之間的5個營運日，以及2025年曆年中的365個營運日）。因此，本公司財務年度結算日為2025年12月31日，其季度營運結果為每季結算日為3月31日、6月30日、9月30日及12月31日。
對於財務年度2024及之前期間，本公司以52週或53週的財務年度結算日為每年12月的最後一個星期四，將財務年度分為三個13週季度及一個包含13週或14週的最終季度。財務年度2024為一個52週年度，包含364個營運日，自2023年12月29日起至2024年12月26日為止。財務年度2023為一個52週年度，包含364個營運日，自2022年12月30日起至2023年12月28日為止。
財務年度2026將為一個包含365個營運日的年度，自2026年1月1日起至2026年12月31日為止，其季度營運結果為每季結算日為3月31日、6月30日、9月30日及12月31日。

本公司第一季通常在酒店及度假村部門產生最弱的營運結果，主要原因為冬季旅遊減少的影響。任何一季的電影產品品質通常會影響本公司電影院部門的營運結果。本公司第二及第三季通常產生最強的營運結果，因為這些期間與電影院產業的典型夏季季節性以及旅館業的夏季強勢時期相符。由於在聖誕節與新年除夕之間的週期通常是本公司電影院部門一年中最強的週期，因此每年12月最後一個星期四的具體時間會歷史性地影響本公司電影院部門第一季及第四季的營運結果。由於財務年度在財務年度2025的轉變，財務年度2025的第一季包含聖誕節與新年除夕之間的5天，而財務年度2025的第四季則包含聖誕節與新年除夕之間的整個週期。

本公司主要營運業務歸屬於兩個業務分部：戲院與飯店及度假村。本管理層討論與分析財務狀況與營運成果（"MD&A"）一般會討論財務年度2025年與財務年度2024年的項目，以及財務年度2025年與財務年度2024年之間的年對年比較。有關財務年度2023年的項目及財務年度2024年與財務年度2023年之間的年對年比較，若未包含於本MD&A中，可參閱本公司財務年度終止於2024年12月26日的10-K年度報告，第二部分，第7項「管理層討論與分析財務狀況與營運成果」。

財務 2024 年度項目及與財務 2025 年度與財務 2024 年度之年對年比較。有關財務 2023 年度項目及與財務 2024 年度與財務 2023 年度之年對年比較，未包含於本 MD&A 之內容，可於本公司 2024 年 12 月 26 日財務年度終結之年度報告 Form 10-K 中，第二部分第七項「管理層對財務狀況及營運成果之討論與分析」中尋得。於本 MD&A 中，總額、 subtotal 及差異數值，可能因四捨五入關係，無法於表格內精確重新計算，因其計算過程係使用未四捨五入之數值。
本公司目前的戰略計畫包括以下目標與策略：戲院
•最大限度利用並發揮我們現有資產。我們在過去十年內已投資約 340 百萬美元，進一步提升新舊戲院的觀影體驗與設施。這些投資包括：

◦DreamLoungerSM 應躺式座椅的增設。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們在 66 家戲院提供所有 DreamLounger 應躺式座椅，約佔本公司自有戲院的 86%。包含我們的豪華大格式（PLF）劇院與應躺式座椅，截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們在約 88% 的本公司自有銀幕提供 DreamLounger 應躺式座椅，我們認為這個比例是全國最大戲院連鎖業者中最高的。

◦UltraScreen DLX®、SuperScreen DLX®（DreamLounger eXperience）與 ScreenX 轉型。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們在 64 家戲院共有 126 個 PLF 銀幕（31 個 UltraScreen DLX 劇院、1 個傳統 UltraScreen® 劇院、87 個 SuperScreen DLX 劇院－螢幕尺寸略小於 UltraScreen，但擁有相同的 DreamLounger 座椅與 Dolby Atmos 音效、4 個 ScreenX 劇院，以及 3 個 IMAX® PLF 銀幕）。在 2023 財年，我們推出了首座 ScreenX 劇院，提供 270 度投影，為顧客帶來沉浸式觀影體驗，並在 2025 財年於其他戲院新增了 3 座 ScreenX 劇院。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們在約 83% 的本公司自有戲院提供至少一個 PLF 銀幕，我們認為這個比例是全國最大戲院連鎖業者中最高的。此外，截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們在約 62% 的本公司自有戲院提供超過一個 PLF 銀幕，我們認為這使我們擁有相當大的運營彈性，透過在戲院的 PLF 銀幕同時放映多部主要電影，以最大化收入，特別是在電影開幕週末及全年高峯時段。我們的 PLF 銀幕通常每銀幕收入較高，且吸引來自較大地理範圍的顧客，我們對顧客收取較高的費用以換取此體驗。

◦調酒與用餐概念。我們持續進一步提升現有劇院內的餐飲服務。我們相信在酒店與餐飲業超過50年的餐飲經驗，使我們擁有獨特的優勢與專業知識，可運用於進一步提升劇院的營收。截至2025年12月31日，我們在48間劇院提供Take Five Lounge、Take Five Express與The Tavern的酒吧/全酒類服務，佔本公司自有劇院約62%。在部分未設置Take Five Lounge據點的場所，我們於Zaffiro's Express據點提供啤酒與葡萄酒。截至2025年12月31日，我們也在39間劇院提供一種或多種大廳用餐概念，包括披薩概念的Zaffiro's® Express與漢堡及其他美式餐點概念的Reel Sizzle，佔約68%
本公司自有的戲院（不含戲院內用餐的戲院）。我們也經營三家 Zaffiro's® Pizzeria and Bar 全服務餐廳。

◦戲院內用餐概念。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們在 20 閣戲院提供完整的飲料與廚師製作的沙拉、三明治、主菜與甜點餐點選擇，佔本公司自有的戲院約 26%，透過兩種服務模式。在 14 閣戲院，我們提供戲院內用餐服務，品牌為 BistroPlex® 和 Movie Tavern by Marcus，消費者可於吧檯、線上、行動應用程式/網頁，以及部分場所由服務員提供點餐，並配送至座位。此外，在 6 閣擁有戲院內用餐服務的戲院，品牌為 Movie Tavern by Marcus 和 Marcus Theatres，我們也提供相同的完整餐點選擇，消費者可於販賣機點餐，並可線上、行動應用程式/網頁訂購配送至座位或至販賣機取餐。

headings: 營運風險
動畫電影的數量與觀眾吸引力不足，可能不利於我們的財務表現。
與電影發行商的關係惡化或發行商合併，可能不利於我們取得商業成功電影的能力，或增加取得這些電影的成本。
可比旅館設施中可用客房的供應量，可能不利於我們的財務表現。
我們各個業務分部及設施均面臨持續激烈的競爭。
勞動力的可得性與成本的變化，可能不利於我們的業務。
供應鏈中斷可能對我們的營運成果產生負面影響。
惡劣天氣條件，特別是在中西部及我們其他市場的冬季，可能不利於我們的財務表現。
本公司營運結果具季節性，導致每季營運成果難以預測且變化幅度大。
本公司資產面臨天災、恐怖攻擊及戰爭等風險，任何上述事件均可能對本公司財務結果造成不利影響。
若透過第三方網路旅遊中介平台所進行之銷售金額大幅增加，消費者對本公司飯店之忠誠度可能下降，進而導致本公司營業收入減少。
財務風險
本公司所處市場若出現不利之經濟情勢，可能對本公司財務結果造成不利影響。
本公司業務屬高度資本密集型，且預開店及開店初期之費用、增加折舊費用及減損費用，可能對本公司財務結果造成不利影響。
本公司可能無法在理想之條件下或任何時間取得所需之資金，亦可能無法透過發行股票或無稀釋現金股東權益之方式取得資金或完成併購交易。
本公司支付股息或回購普通股之能力可能受到限制或有其他限制。
我們的債務償還需要大量現金，而我們可能無法從業務中產生足夠的現金流量來償還債務。
戰略風險
我們可能無法實現戰略計畫與併購所預期的效益與績效。
我們辨識合適不動產以取得、開發及管理的能力，將直接影響我們達成部分成長目標的能力。
我們辨識合適合資夥伴或籌集投資資金以取得、開發及管理飯店與度假村的能力，將直接影響我們達成部分成長目標的能力。
透過合資或合夥關係進行投資會降低我們管理風險的能力。
法律、法規與合規風險
食品產品召回及相關成本可能對我們的聲譽與財務狀況造成不利影響。
本公司受重大政府規範管制，可能導致重大成本。
本公司受複雜稅務規範管制，可能因稅率變動、新稅法實施或面臨額外稅務負擔而受影響。
一般風險
本公司股票價格可能波動，可能導致股東對本公司提起證券集體訴訟。
本公司章程、組織規則及威斯康辛州法律的某些條款，可能阻止股東認為有利的收購，也可能降低本公司股票的市場價格。
paragraphs: 下列風險因素及其他資訊包含於本年度報告表 10-K 中，應謹慎考量。上述所描述的風險與不確定性並非我們唯一面臨的風險。尚有其他風險與不確定性，目前我們尚未知悉或認為不重要，也可能影響我們的業務運作。若任何上述風險發生，將可能對我們的業務、財務狀況、營運結果與現金流造成重大不利影響。
疫情或大流行可能對我們的戲院與飯店及度假村業務、營運結果、流動性、現金流、財務狀況、取得信貸市場的管道與償還現有及未來債務的能力造成重大不利影響，未來的疫情或大流行也可能在未來造成類似重大不利影響。

冠狀病毒（COVID-19）疫情對我們的兩個業務部門造成了前所未有的影響。作為一家經營電影院、飯店及度假村、餐廳與酒吧的公司，這些業務皆包含顧客與遊客聚集的空間，因此我們的業務因政府為控制疫情而採取的防範措施而受到顯著影響。這些措施包括，但不僅限於，宣佈國家及州級緊急狀態、鼓勵社交距離、限制行動與聚集自由、強制關閉非必要商業活動及/或限制容量、發布居家隔離、隔離與居家待命命令，以及發布口罩及/或疫苗強制規定。
我們無法預測未來是否會再次發生類似或不同的疫情或大流行。傳染病爆發的時間越長且越嚴重，包括重複或週期性爆發或未來的疫情或大流行，對我們的業務、營運結果、流動性、現金流、財務狀況、取得信貸市場的管道與償還現有及未來債務的能力造成的不利影響將越嚴重。

對未來疫情的擔憂與關注可能導致顧客再次避免在公共空間聚集，即使在沒有政府指令或限制的情況下。我們對未來因疫情或大流行而導致的戲院與飯店及度假村關閉或限制措施的持續時間毫無控制力，也無法預測。若我們因未來長時間關閉而無法產生收入，這將對我們遵守債務契約、履行付款義務及資本項目資金需求的能力造成負面影響。在這種情況下，我們將尋求契約寬限或嘗試修改債務契約，但我們無法保證這些努力會成功。若我們未能成功，貸款人可能宣佈違約並要求立即償還根據信貸協議及優先債券所欠的金額，這可能對我們經營業務的能力造成重大不利影響。此外，我們可能透過發行新債務或股票來尋求額外流動性。我們能否取得額外融資及任何額外融資的條件，部分取決於我們無法控制的因素，我們可能無法在可接受的條件下或完全無法取得額外融資。

我們的電影院業務及電影產業整體的財務表現，高度依賴於可供觀賞電影的普遍吸引力，以及製片廠的宣傳、廣告與支持活動，而這些因素我們無法控制。我們的電影院業務的相對成功將持續取決於製片廠及其他製片者所提供的電影數量與吸引力。電影表現不佳、因演員、作家或導演罷工等事件導致電影製作中斷，或電影發行商對其電影的宣傳努力減少，都可能對我們的業務與營運結果造成不利影響。我們的產業在 COVID-19 疫情後的幾年中，經歷了可供觀賞電影數量顯著減少。在財務年度 2023 年及 2024 年，可供觀賞的新電影數量因財務年度 2023 年發生的美國作家協會（WGA）及電視與廣播藝術家協會 - 美國電視與廣播藝術家協會（SAG-AFTRA）罷工而受到負面影響。製片廠也可能決定某些類型的電影不會在電影院上映，而是直接上線流媒體服務，進一步影響可供觀賞的電影數量。此外，我們的季度營運結果極度依賴於每個季度我們所放映的電影數量與吸引力。因此，我們的季度結果可能難以預測且較為波動。
